Voat needs the technical ability to segregate users, so that certain users can still access the site even while the majority are being denied access or given a read only or otherwise limited use of the site. Priority should be given to those with the highest karma, as they produce the content and drive the site... however, users should be able to buy priority access with bitcoin... rather than using donations... bitcoiners can fund the site and those who contribute the most will have greatest access to the site even during meltdowns.

I am spanish. Our most famous "news aggregator" website is called Meneame (meneame.net) founded in 2005. It has a lot of traffic, in the spanish context, it is not a "small website".

Something they did around 6-7 years ago was to make all upvotes and downvotes public.

For example, the most voted news at the moment: https://www.meneame.net/story/dimite-yanis-varoufakis-ministro-finanzas-eng

It has 1619 upvotes and the link received around 10k clicks. If you go to any of the comments, near where it says votos you will see a number. If you click on this number, you will see who voted it positive, and who voted it negative.

This is an excellent tool to track spammers, astrosurfers, vote brigrading... or whoever wants to game the system. It also makes you think twice about what you vote, especially in the case of a downvote. For any user you can go to his/her profile and see his last upvotes or downvotes.

Also, each user has a karma value, which is a numbet between 0 and 20. When you upvote or downvote something, instead if being a single unit, it's your karma. Your karma goes up or down depending on the quality of your voting. basically if you upvote something and then this thing is highly upvoted you gain karma, the same the other way around. Voting something that is already highly voted is kind of meaningless, apart from adding or substracting your karma from there.

They also have excellent algorithms to track vote brigading. I recommend you look into their github:

https://github.com/gallir/Meneame

Anyway, I know at first making upvotes and downvotes public may make people crazy, but it did work very well there.

Basic info- Crusader Kings II is a fun Grand Strategy game, the basic gist is to maintain a dynasty from 1066-1452(ish). You play as a dynasty rather than a singular character, and you're left with trying to survive and expand your powerbase in the medieval world via conquest and dynastic alliances. The game ends either at the last date possible, or if you're entire dynasty dies or becomes landless.

A bit more details: The game gives you a lot of options, with no real story bar Charlemagne due to his personal events with relations to his wife(if she is a lombard princess), and his family(specifically his brother/mother; albeit there is an event to legitimize his bastards) The game is effectively divided into 4 playable tiers; Count, Duke, King, and Emperor. Count being the lowest and Emperor the highest. The game involves a lot of plotting, fabricating claims, killing your enemies, brothers, fathers, mothers, sons, daughters, cousins, grandsons, granddaughters, etc. Expansion involves getting claims either by marrying someone or fabricating one. Or, if you are on the border with a different religious group, fighting infidels, or heathens for their territories. While the game is fun, a lot of the dlc tends to break the game for a bit; specifically Way of Life has created a lot of talking points due to the clutter of a significant amount of bastards in the game files since. It may look daunting, but the game is rather simple once you understand the basic mechanics of it.
Due to the randomness of how AI sometimes act, and some of the great mods for it, the game can give you a good amount of playtime. I'd recommend it if you're willing to sit for long periods of time, especially at the beginning to learn it.
